hook: Nearly 7,000 square miles of Chile's Atacama Desert just carpeted in wildflowers.

sections.voiceover: Nearly 7,000 square miles of Chile's Atacama Desert just carpeted in wildflowers.

sections.voiceover: In 2026, heavy winter rain from an El Niño super cycle flooded Copiapó. Did heavy winter rains bring Copiapó its highest rainfall since records began in the 1950s?
b_roll: map pinpointing Copiapó Chile with rain radar overlay

sections.voiceover: However, Live Science reported on October 2, 2026, that El Niño awakened millions of seeds and bulbs.
b_roll: macro shot of dormant desert seeds sprouting after heavy downpours

sections.voiceover: The barren landscape across Chile transformed into a massive floral display. Nearly 7,000 square miles of land now stretch in full color.
b_roll: panoramic satellite view of the Atacama landscape bursting in color
